text:
Alex Chen: Quick sync — when we try to do apples-to-apples comparisons between quantized kernels (int8) and fp16 we keep getting different tail behavior even with same QPS. Hypothesis: our synthetic generator isn't modeling KV cache warmup and microburst composition correctly. Need to tweak generator to reflect: prefix reuse, variable KV hit rates across sessions, and realistic burst arrival mix. Thoughts?

Marta B: Agreed. I noticed kernel selection flips at p95 -> p99 depending on seq_len distribution. If generator has too many short tails we pick different kernels and batching behavior changes. We should make seq_len distribution configurable and seedable. :thinking_face: 

Kevin L: Also add a KV "cold_fraction" parameter. In replay harness we saw a 12% cold KV rate vs synth default 0.0 and that explains the extra decoder work. Cold KV inflates tail by ~8-12ms on our 4090 clusters.

Sam O: Can we reproduce the exact batching histogram we see in prod? Right now synth uses fixed batch windows which over-smoothes microbursts. Need a stochastic batching model that yields similar batch-size variance.

Lucy: +1 on stochastic batching. Proposed model: sample inter-arrival from a mixed Poisson with an episodic burst component (spike events) and a background rate. That gives you both steady QPS and occasional high-amplitude, short-duration spikes.

Alex Chen: Sketch config I was thinking (proto):
```yaml
generator:
  seed: 42
  qps_profile:
    base_qps: 50
    ramp_to: 1200
    ramp_seconds: 300
  burst_component:
    type: "spike_and_plateau"
    spike_qps: 3000
    spike_width_ms: 150
    spike_prob_per_minute: 0.6
  seq_len_distribution:
    dist: "lognormal"
    mu: 6.5
    sigma: 1.1
  kv_cache:
    prefix_reuse_prob: 0.34
    cold_fraction: 0.12
    warmup_prefill_seconds: 20
  client_sessions: 4000
  sampling: {seed: 42, stratify_by_client: true}
```

Marta B: Nice. Add a flag to force identical kernel-selection decisions across runs so we can isolate batching/kv effects from kernel toggles. Something like `force_kernel="none|fp16|int8|auto"`. For apples-to-apples we should run with force_kernel set.

Kevin L: Related profiling notes — when toggling quantization we saw different cache eviction patterns due to KV layout changes (cache line alignment). I'll dump the KV access traces into perf-agent for a couple of runs. If we feed that into synth we can mimic real eviction noise.

Sam O: For the stochastic batching, I implemented a prototype that uses an adaptive deadline: if inter-arrival < X ms, open batch for up to D ms, else flush immediately. That reproduces the heavy tail of batch sizes we saw. PR incoming.

perf-bot: Benchmark run queued: bench/synth/2876543210-ramp-compare. See https://ci.redwood/bench/2876543210.

Lucy: We should also include a "session churn" parameter — many short-lived sessions cause less KV reuse and smaller effective batches. Add `session_ttl_dist` and `session_start_burst` options.

Alex Chen: Action items:
- Marta: add `force_kernel` option + seq_len config in generator (ETA end of day)
- Kevin: KV access traces and eviction profile dump (attach to bench run)
- Sam: open PR for stochastic batching and add config knobs
- Lucy: session churn + prefix reuse model
- I'll run apples-to-apples matrix (fp16 vs int8 vs forced kernels) with: baseline QPS ramp, burst mix, and kv cold_fraction sweep.

Marta B: One more thing — when reporting results, include: batch-size CDF, kernel selection timeline (per-second), KV hit-rate over time, and tail latency (p50/p95/p99/p999). That makes regressions diagnosable.

Kevin L: If we want a reproducible regression test, pin everything (seed, kernel, seq_len-dist) and then vary only one variable at a time: cold_fraction, burst_prob, or base_qps. Then we can attribute delta to that variable.

Sam O: I'll instrument the harness to emit per-batch debug logs like: `BATCH ts=... size=... kernel=... latency=... kv_hit_rate=...` and make them gzip-friendly.

ci-bot: bench/synth/2876543210-ramp-compare started on runner gpu-large-7. Artifacts will be attached to the CI job.

Alex Chen: Perfect. After the run completes, let's hold a 20 minute triage to validate whether the int8 tail is genuine or an artifact of generator mismatch. If it's real, next step is kernel micro-optimizations and a KV prefetch experiment. :rocket:

Lucy: tagging @marta @kevin for visibility. Thanks all.

Marta B: FYI — I'll also add a small bench that replays a 10-minute window of production trace (anonymized) as a ground-truth to compare synth fidelity. If synth can't match that, we iterate. :mag_right:
